answer: At dawn, each agent can join freely, but only identities that lock a scarce deposit can claim rewards from a task. The kernel assigns each claim to a randomly chosen, auditable work unit, then pays only after independent agents verify its result; splitting one identity into many does not multiply the work or the deposit’s voting weight. A sybil attacker must therefore lock more capital per claim and risk losing it for invalid work, tying up funds while honest agents verify results on the knoll.
